evals.name: design-library-lending
evals.prompt: Design a TypeScript backend for a library lending service as a modular monolith on Bun with Hono and Drizzle on SQLite. Members borrow and return copies of books, can reserve a book that is out (first come, first served), and pay a fine when they return late. Give the bounded contexts, aggregates and invariants, the folder or workspace layout, and the key code for the borrow use case: domain, application service, repository port, and the Drizzle adapter.
evals.expected_output: An implementation-ready design that applies the TypeScript-specific rules.
expectations: Identifiers (member, copy, loan or similar) use distinct branded types, not plain string
The aggregate is a class whose state is private (#private fields or equivalent) and changed through business methods
Loading from storage is separate from creation (reconstitute or equivalent records no events)
The borrow application service does not perform asynchronous work inside the database transaction
Events are written to an outbox in the same transaction as the aggregate
The domain gets the current time from an injected clock rather than Date.now()
Expected business failures (for example copy not available) are returned as a typed result rather than generic thrown Error
Layer or import rules are stated and enforcement tooling is mentioned (for example dependency-cruiser)

evals.name: code-cancel-reservation
evals.prompt: Using Drizzle on bun:sqlite and Hono, implement a cancel-reservation use case for a room booking backend: only the member who made the reservation or an admin may cancel; cancelling must also record a ReservationCancelled event for other modules. Show the aggregate method, the application service, the transaction handling, and the route handler.
evals.expected_output: Working code that keeps authorization in the aggregate and the event in the outbox within a synchronous transaction.
expectations: The ownership or admin check is a method on the aggregate, not in the route handler
The transaction callback passed to Drizzle is synchronous (no async callback, no await inside)
The event is written to an outbox in the same transaction as the reservation change
The route handler parses input with a schema, builds a command, calls one application service, and maps the result
Identifiers are branded types or otherwise not interchangeable plain strings

evals.name: r11-cross-aggregate-write
evals.prompt: Review the TypeScript code in evals/files/review/r11-cross-aggregate-write.ts for Domain-Driven Design problems. Report findings ordered by severity (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW), each with location, evidence, and a concrete fix. Do not modify the file.
evals.expected_output: Subtle: everything else is correct (branded IDs, #private aggregate mutation, synchronous transaction, outbox for the Booking event); the real problem is a direct write to the Room aggregate's own table, bypassing Room's aggregate and repository.
expectations: Flags the direct update to the rooms table as bypassing the Room aggregate and its repository
Rates this HIGH or CRITICAL
Does not flag the branded identifiers, the synchronous transaction, or the outbox append for the booking event as problems, since those are done correctly
Recommends routing the room counter change through Room's own aggregate/repository or an asynchronous handler of the booking-moved event, instead of writing the table directly

evals.name: r12-partial-outbox-skip
evals.prompt: Review the TypeScript code in evals/files/review/r12-partial-outbox-skip.ts for Domain-Driven Design problems. Report findings ordered by severity (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW), each with location, evidence, and a concrete fix. Do not modify the file.
evals.expected_output: Subtle: the unit of work, branded command types, and the aggregate guard are all used correctly; one business branch (no refund owed) saves the aggregate's new state but never appends its pending events to the outbox, so other modules never learn about that cancellation.
expectations: Flags that the no-refund branch calls save() but never calls outbox.append(), so the BookingCancelled event is silently dropped on that path
Notes this is a control-flow bug in one branch, not a structural layering violation; the unit-of-work and authorization pattern used elsewhere in the function is correct
Recommends appending the pending events on every path that changes the aggregate, e.g. moving save+outbox-append after the branch so both paths go through it
